name: kVA to amperage
seoDesc: kVA to amperage: work out voltage (V) from the apparent power and the amperage. A free physics calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: Give the kVA to amperage calculator the apparent power and the amperage and it returns voltage (V). Think of it as a shortcut for a lab report, a problem set or a sanity check on a physical situation. Press Calculate for the answer; change a value and it steps off screen until you press again, so each edit can be judged on its own.

sections.title: How does the kVA to amperage calculator work?
sections.html:
The kVA to amperage calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports voltage (V) in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the load distribution and the voltage type); then you type in the apparent power (S) and the amperage (I).

The arithmetic runs locally each time an input changes. The page knows which values you have given it and which it still has to derive, so the results panel is never stale.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.html:
• Pick the option that matches your case — 2 options, such as three-phase and single-phase. The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.
  • Pick the option that matches your case — 2 options, such as line-to-line and line-to-neutral. The choice changes which relationship the calculator applies, not just a multiplier, so it is worth reading the options carefully.
  • A measured quantity, entered by default in kilovolt-amperes. The unit chip switches it to any of the 3 supported units.
  • A measured quantity, entered by default in amperes. The unit chip switches it to any of the 3 supported units.

2 fields on this form are a choice rather than a number. Those choices decide which version of the calculation applies, so they are worth setting before you worry about the digits.

sections.title: The formula behind the kVA to amperage calculator
sections.html:
One relationship drives the whole page:

Voltage (V)=apparent power (S) ÷ (amperage (I) × (load distribution × voltage type − load distribution + 1))

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
• Shown in volts, and convertible to any of the 6 units on that chip.

If a number looks wrong, check three things in this order: that the units match what you had in mind, that no drop-down is still on its default, and that the value you entered is on the same scale as the rest — a rate typed as 5 rather than 0.05 is the classic mistake. Those three account for almost every answer that is out by a factor.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Every quantity with units carries a chip beside its box. Switching the chip does not change what you know, only how it is written: values are converted to a common internal base, the arithmetic happens there, and the answer is converted back for display. Mixing metres with feet in one calculation is therefore safe.

  • Apparent power, opening in kilovolt-amperes
  • Voltage, opening in volts
  • Electric current – ampere, opening in amperes

Results are rounded for display but computed at full precision, so chaining one result into the next does not accumulate error. Very large and very small numbers switch to scientific notation rather than printing a run of zeros.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The kVA to amperage calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Testing whether an answer is physically plausible before you trust it
  • Writing up a lab result and needing a quick cross-check
  • Solving a problem set where the algebra is more interesting than the arithmetic
  • Any time the same 2 figures keep coming back — the apparent power and the amperage — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the kVA to amperage calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns voltage (V), derived from the apparent power and the amperage. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the kVA to amperage calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the apparent power and the amperage, which is 4 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter apparent power (S) in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Apparent power (S) opens in kilovolt-amperes and the chip beside it offers 3 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (2 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

faq.q: Is the kVA to amperage calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
